blocks.prompt: 8 (i)(a) How many (a) diagonals and (b) triangles can be formed by joining the vertices of the polygon having: (i) 5 sides? Part (a): diagonals.
blocks.explanation:
A pentagon has 5 vertices. Any two vertices joined give a line segment; those segments are either sides or diagonals.
We must count the diagonals.
Plan: count all pairs \({}^{5}C_{2}\), then subtract the 5 sides.
steps:
Given: a polygon with 5 sides, so 5 vertices (no three in a line).
To find: the number of diagonals.
Method: A segment is fixed by its two end points, and AB is the same as BA, so segments are combinations of 2 vertices. Then remove the sides.

Count all segments
\[{}^{5}C_{2} = \dfrac{5 \cdot 4}{2} = 10\]
Why: Each pair of vertices gives exactly one segment.

Subtract the sides
\[10 - 5 = 5\]
Why: 5 of these segments are sides of the polygon, not diagonals.

Check with the formula
\[\dfrac{n(n-3)}{2} = \dfrac{5 \times 2}{2}\]
\[= 5 \;\checkmark\]
Why: From each vertex, diagonals go to the \(n - 3\) vertices that are not itself or its two neighbours; each diagonal is counted from both ends, so divide by 2.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The question asks for (a) diagonals and (b) triangles for each of the 3 polygons, so 6 answers. The answer key prints only 3: i) 10, ii) 20, iii) 54. 20 and 54 are the diagonals of the 8-sided and 12-sided polygons, but a pentagon has 5 diagonals, not 10 (10 is its number of triangles). Correct: diagonals 5, 20, 54; triangles 10, 56, 220.

blocks.prompt: 8 (i)(b) How many (a) diagonals and (b) triangles can be formed by joining the vertices of the polygon having: (i) 5 sides? Part (b): triangles.
blocks.explanation:
Any 3 vertices of the pentagon (no three in a line) make one triangle.
We must count the triangles.
Plan: \({}^{5}C_{3}\).
steps:
Given: 5 vertices.
To find: the number of triangles with vertices at these points.
Method: A triangle is fixed by its 3 corners; ABC, BCA, ... are the same triangle, so use combinations of 3.

Choose 3 vertices
\[{}^{5}C_{3} = \dfrac{5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3}{6} = 10\]
Why: 3 factors counting down from 5, divided by \(3! = 6\).

Check
\[{}^{5}P_{3} \div 3! = 60 \div 6 = 10 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Ordered triples count each triangle \(3! = 6\) times.
